item.title: Intel Invests €5 Billion in Irish Hub to Keep Up in AI Chip Race
item.description: Intel Corp. is spending €5 billion ($5.7 billion) to expand its plant in Ireland, as the chipmaker attempts to regain its manufacturing dominance for the AI boom.

item.title: Bangladesh Is a Nuclear Power Test Case for Developing Nations
item.description: Atomic energy offers emerging economies a way to wean themselves off imported fossil fuels, but it also has downsides.

item.title: Saudi Energy Minister’s Influence Grows With Industry Portfolio
item.description: Saudi Arabian Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman was appointed minister of industry and mineral resources in addition to his current post, signaling an expanded role for the royal and closer integration of the two sectors.

item.title: Renewed Iran Woes Flip Script for Traders Betting War Risks Over
item.description: A day after making an investment call tied to subsiding Middle East tensions, BCA Research’s Marko Papic had to scrap his recommendation at a loss. Donald Trump had said the war in Iran was back on.

item.title: ChatGPT’s Upgraded Voice Mode Captures the Imperfections of Real Conversations
item.description: The OpenAI chatbot now speaks and converses a lot more like a real person

item.title: Washington Is Looking to Keep China From Training Its AI on US Models
item.description: Anthropic and OpenAI’s warnings about “adversarial distillation” are reinvigorating one of the oldest debates in Silicon Valley.

item.title: A Summer Reading List to Grasp the Geopolitical Shifts Shaping the Future
item.description: US Treasury’s Bessent lays out a ‘doctrine’ steeped in economic self-reliance

item.title: Why Global Economy’s Resilience May Rise With Diminished Dollar Dominance
item.description: The decline in the dollar’s role reduces ripples of stress through the world in times of crisis

item.title: Chile Debt Sale Window Opens as Investors Ignore Mounting Risks
item.description: Chile’s government has a window of opportunity to sell debt abroad as sovereign spreads hover near two-decade lows, with investors shrugging off an escalation in the Middle East conflict, domestic debt woes and a stagnating economy.

item.title: US Cost for Gas Power at 17-Year High and Climbing, Lazard Says
item.description: The cost of power from natural gas-fired plants in the US hit the highest level in at least 17 years, and is poised to climb even higher as demand surges from new data centers.

item.title: India Inflation Tops RBI Target for First Time in 17 Months
item.description: India’s inflation accelerated last month, rising above the Reserve Bank of India’s target for the first time in nearly a year and a half and keeping policymakers on guard.

item.title: Researchers Raise Concerns That AI May Atrophy Human Skills
item.description: Will we end up with a generation of experts in high-stakes professions who never build true expertise?

item.title: Investors Expect ‘Sunshine and Rainbows’ This Earnings Season
item.description: Estimates are running up against sticky inflation and rising odds of interest rate hikes. With stocks near records, there’s little room for error.

item.title: Apple’s $600 Billion Rally Fueled by Traders Fleeing AI Selloff
item.description: Investors are flocking back to Apple Inc. as nervousness about artificial intelligence spending weighs on the stocks of chipmakers and cloud-computing giants.

item.title: Maker of Soya Supreme Cooking Oil Plans Pakistan IPO This Month
item.description: Cooking oil manufacturer Agro Processors & Atmospheric Gases Ltd. is planning an initial public offering in Pakistan this month to finance a plant expansion, adding to a record year for listings in the country.

item.title: Who’s Scamming the Scammers?
item.description: Scambaiting is one way the fed-up masses are dealing with a flood of fraud.

item.title: CLO Fund’s 50% Tumble Fuels Power Struggle That Spills Into Open
item.description: A fight over who gets to run a $580 million credit fund has erupted into an unusually public Wall Street brawl, pitting claims of poor performance against accusations of a cash grab ahead of a proxy vote later this month.

item.title: Wall Street to Warsh: Skip the Guidance, But Tell Us What You Think About the Economy
item.description: In his zeal to avoid signaling where interest rates are headed, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh has obscured something else that’s crucial to investors, analysts and other policymakers: How he would react when challenged by the economy.

item.title: Deutsche Bank Boosts Gulf Team With Standard Chartered Hires
item.description: Deutsche Bank AG is expanding its private banking business in Dubai with a series of hires from Standard Chartered Plc, further deepening its presence in the Middle East despite the regional conflict.

item.title: Dyson’s New $100 Portable Fan Is Beating the Heat — and Sales Expectations
item.description: The newest status symbol on the streets of Manhattan is a high-tech portable fan that’s been hard to get hold of.

item.title: Meta’s Louisiana Data Center to Surpass $250 Billion Price Tag
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. has committed to spending an additional $40 billion on its sprawling data center campus in Louisiana, pushing its total expected investment beyond $250 billion for the site as it continues to grow its artificial intelligence computing footprint.

item.title: Saudi Tech Firm NourNet Is Said to Pick Goldman, HSBC for IPO
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s NourNet is working with Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and HSBC Holdings Plc on a potential initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter, adding to a pipeline of Gulf listings despite the regional conflict.

item.title: Fed’s Bowman Urges Global Financial Watchdog to be Flexible
item.description: The Federal Reserve’s top bank cop warned the Financial Stability Board against enforcing “strict rules” that are not suitable for a diverse group of countries, saying those efforts can erode the international watchdog’s effectiveness.

item.title: India Trade Deficit Widens as Hormuz Risks Cloud Outlook
item.description: India’s trade deficit widened in June, with uncertainty over the US-Iran conflict and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz continuing to cloud the outlook for global supply chains.

item.title: James Bond Studio Pinewood in Talks on Sterling Debt Sale
item.description: The UK film and TV studio behind the James Bond movies is meeting with investors ahead of a possible sale of sterling-denominated notes.

item.title: De Beers to Shutter South African Diamond Mine to Save Cash
item.description: Diamond giant De Beers plans to halt production at its South African mine for two years, as the one-time monopoly continues to wrestle with one of the deepest crises to ever hit the industry.

item.title: UAE Steps Up Moves to Help Term Buyers Avoid Hormuz Transits
item.description: Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. is broadening the options for long-term customers to take offshore oil from outside the Strait of Hormuz, stepping up efforts that enable buyers to circumvent the chokepoint.

item.title: As Milei’s Aura Fades, Argentina Starts to Look for a Third Way
item.description: Corruption was once Javier Milei’s strongest card against the Peronist movement that dominated Argentine politics for decades. Now it’s just one of several vulnerabilities that are damaging the libertarian president’s brand and giving wings to the opposition’s comeback plans.

item.title: Indonesia Avoids S&P Rating Outlook Cut in Win for Prabowo
item.description: Indonesia retained its investment-grade rating and stable outlook at S&P Global Ratings, a reprieve for President Prabowo Subianto and his fiscal policy credibility after a bond market selloff in June.

item.title: German Tax Trades Fallout May Cost Firms €7 Billion, BaFin Says
item.description: German financial watchdog BaFin said financial companies that engaged in two controversial strategies to game dividend taxes are facing related legal and fiscal liabilities of as much €7.01 billion ($7.99 billion).
